# Configuration reference

This page lists every configuration key with its type, built-in default and the environment variable that overrides it. It is generated from the code (`internal/config` and the packages whose settings it embeds), so it cannot drift from what the server reads. For the load order (defaults, then the YAML file, then the environment), validation and how to start the server with a file, see [Configuration](../getting-started/configuration.md). Annotated copies of every key are in [`openartifact.example.yaml`](../../openartifact.example.yaml) and [`.env.example`](../../.env.example).

- **YAML key**: the dotted path in the configuration file; `server.port` is `port` under `server:`.
- **Env**: the environment variable that overrides the key; it takes precedence over the file. When several variables are listed, they are aliases and the first one that is set wins.
- **Type**: `string`, `int`, `bool`, `float`, `duration` (Go syntax such as `5m` or `90s`), `list` (a YAML sequence; comma-separated in the environment) or `map` (a YAML mapping; comma-separated `key=value` pairs in the environment).
- **Default**: the value used when neither the file nor the environment sets the key; `empty` is an empty string, list or map.
- Credentials are marked **Secret**: keep them in environment variables or in a file only the server can read.

## Top level

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | `BASE_URL` | string | `http://localhost:8080` | `baseUrl` is the public URL of the server; it is used for generated links and SSO callbacks, so set it when the server runs behind a reverse proxy. |

## server

`server` configures the HTTP listener, TLS, timeouts and request limits.

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `server.host` | `SERVER_HOST` | string | `0.0.0.0` | `host` is the listen address. |
| `server.port` | `SERVER_PORT` | int | `8080` | `port` is the listen port. |
| `server.readTimeout` | `SERVER_READ_TIMEOUT` | int | `0` | `readTimeout` bounds an entire request (headers + body), in seconds. 0 (the default) means no limit so large artifact uploads are never truncated; slowloris protection instead comes from readHeaderTimeout. |
| `server.writeTimeout` | `SERVER_WRITE_TIMEOUT` | int | `0` | `writeTimeout` bounds writing the response, in seconds. 0 (the default) means no limit: large artifact downloads and streams rely on per-handler deadlines instead of one server-wide cutoff. |
| `server.readHeaderTimeout` | `SERVER_READ_HEADER_TIMEOUT` | int | `20` | `readHeaderTimeout` bounds only the time to read request headers, in seconds. It stays short regardless of readTimeout to still mitigate slowloris-style attacks even when body reads are unbounded. |
| `server.maxBodyBytes` | `SERVER_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | int | `17179869184` | `maxBodyBytes` caps the body of every request (http.MaxBytesReader), a last line of defence behind the per-handler limits so no endpoint can be made to spool or buffer an unbounded body. 0 disables the cap. |
| `server.shutdownTimeout` | `SERVER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` | int | `30` | `shutdownTimeout` is how many seconds in-flight requests get to finish during a graceful shutdown. |
| `server.tlsEnabled` | `SERVER_TLS_ENABLED` | bool | `false` | `tlsEnabled` serves HTTPS and sends HSTS; it requires tlsCert and tlsKey. |
| `server.tlsCert` | `SERVER_TLS_CERT` | string | `empty` | `tlsCert` is the path of the PEM certificate file. |
| `server.tlsKey` | `SERVER_TLS_KEY` | string | `empty` | `tlsKey` is the path of the PEM private key file. |
| `server.apiKey` | `API_KEY` | string | `empty` | **Secret.** `apiKey` is a deprecated static key accepted on write endpoints while auth.legacyApiKeyEnabled is true. It authenticates as system/legacy-api-key and logs a warning on each use; empty disables it. |
| `server.corsOrigins` | `CORS_ORIGINS` | list | `empty` | `corsOrigins` lists the browser origins allowed by CORS; none by default. |
| `server.instanceId` | `OPENARTIFACT_INSTANCE_ID` | string | `empty` | `instanceId` names this instance in HA deployments; /health reports it (omitted when empty, the hostname is never disclosed). |
| `server.ipAllowlist` | `OPENARTIFACT_IP_ALLOWLIST` | list | `empty` | `ipAllowlist` lists the CIDR blocks allowed to connect; empty allows all. |
| `server.rateLimitRps` | `OPENARTIFACT_RATE_LIMIT_RPS` | int | `0` | `rateLimitRps` caps requests per second per client IP; 0 disables the limit. |
| `server.trustedProxies` | `OPENARTIFACT_TRUSTED_PROXIES` | list | `empty` | `trustedProxies` lists CIDR blocks of reverse proxies allowed to set X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP. Empty (default) means no proxy is trusted — the immediate TCP peer is always used as the client IP, so a client can never spoof its own IP via those headers. |
| `server.pprofEnabled` | `OPENARTIFACT_PPROF_ENABLED` | bool | `false` | `pprofEnabled` mounts Go's runtime profiler under /api/v1/admin/pprof/ (admin "manage" permission required). Off by default: profiles expose internals and CPU profiling costs cycles. Sets non-zero mutex and block profile rates while enabled. |

## database

`database` configures the PostgreSQL connection and its pool.

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `database.driver` | `DB_DRIVER` | string | `postgres` | `driver` names the database driver. It must be non-empty; PostgreSQL is the only supported database and the server always connects to it. |
| `database.host` | `DB_HOST` | string | `localhost` | `host` is the database host. |
| `database.port` | `DB_PORT` | int | `5432` | `port` is the database port. |
| `database.user` | `DB_USER` | string | `postgres` | `user` is the database user. |
| `database.password` | `DB_PASSWORD` | string | `empty` | **Secret.** `password` is the database password. The `CHANGE_ME` placeholder of the example files is rejected at startup. |
| `database.database` | `DB_NAME` | string | `artifact_repo` | `database` is the database name. |
| `database.sslMode` | `DB_SSLMODE` | string | `require` | `sslMode` is the PostgreSQL sslmode; disable only for local development without TLS. |
| `database.options` | `DB_OPTIONS` | map | `empty` | `options` are extra libpq connection parameters. The environment form is comma-separated key=value pairs, merged over the YAML keys. |
| `database.maxOpenConns` | `DB_MAX_OPEN_CONNS` | int | `25` | `maxOpenConns` is the size of the connection pool. 0 means the driver default; otherwise at least 2 (a blob-lock transaction pins one connection and its callback needs another), and at least 4 while tiering.enabled is true. |
| `database.maxIdleConns` | `DB_MAX_IDLE_CONNS` | int | `5` | `maxIdleConns` is how many idle connections the pool keeps warm. |
| `database.connMaxLifetimeMinutes` | `DB_CONN_MAX_LIFETIME_MINUTES` | int | `30` | `connMaxLifetimeMinutes` is the maximum lifetime of a connection, in minutes. |
| `database.authCacheTtlMs` | `DB_AUTH_CACHE_TTL_MS` | int | `2000` | `authCacheTtlMs` is how long, in milliseconds, per-request authentication lookups (token, user, groups, permission targets, repository by name) are served from memory. Writes through this process invalidate immediately; other replicas observe a change after at most this long. 0 disables the cache. |
| `database.connectTimeout` | `DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` | duration | `1m` | `connectTimeout` is how long startup keeps retrying the initial database connection (capped exponential backoff) before giving up. 0 fails at the first error. |

## storage

`storage` selects and configures the blob store (see [operations/storage.md](../operations/storage.md)). Its replica block adds an asynchronous second copy of every blob (see [operations/replication.md](../operations/replication.md)).

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `storage.type` | `STORAGE_BACKEND`, `STORAGE_TYPE` | string | `filesystem` | `type` selects the storage backend: filesystem, s3, gcs, azure, garage, seaweedfs or oci. garage and seaweedfs reuse the S3 client with path-style addressing forced on. |
| `storage.endpoint` | `STORAGE_ENDPOINT` | string | `empty` | `endpoint` is the endpoint URL of an S3-compatible service (s3, garage, seaweedfs) or the URL of the OCI registry. |
| `storage.bucket` | `STORAGE_BUCKET` | string | `artifacts` | `bucket` is the bucket name (s3, garage, seaweedfs) or the OCI repository prefix. |
| `storage.region` | `STORAGE_REGION` | string | `us-east-1` | `region` is the AWS region or equivalent. |
| `storage.accessKey` | `STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY` | string | `empty` | `accessKey` is the S3 access key. It is used only when both keys are set, otherwise the AWS credential chain applies. |
| `storage.secretKey` | `STORAGE_SECRET_KEY` | string | `empty` | **Secret.** `secretKey` is the S3 secret key. |
| `storage.path` | `STORAGE_PATH` | string | `/var/lib/artifacts` | `path` is the directory of the filesystem backend. |
| `storage.options` | `STORAGE_OPTIONS` | map | `empty` | `options` are free-form backend options. The environment form is comma-separated key=value pairs, merged over the YAML keys. None of the built-in backends reads any key yet. |
| `storage.forcePathStyle` | `STORAGE_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE` | bool | `false` | `forcePathStyle` uses path-style S3 addressing (required for MinIO, Garage and SeaweedFS). |
| `storage.presignTtl` | `STORAGE_S3_PRESIGN_TTL` | duration | `5m` | `presignTtl` is the lifetime of presigned download URLs (s3, gcs), clamped to 1m-1h. It only applies while presignDownloads is on. |
| `storage.presignUploadTtl` | `STORAGE_PRESIGN_UPLOAD_TTL` | duration | `30m` | `presignUploadTtl` is the lifetime of presigned PUT upload URLs, clamped to 1m-12h. |
| `storage.presignMaxPendingUploads` | `STORAGE_PRESIGN_MAX_PENDING_UPLOADS` | int | `20` | `presignMaxPendingUploads` is how many outstanding (not completed, not expired) presigned uploads one user may hold; 0 means unlimited. Beyond it, creating an upload answers 429. |
| `storage.presignDownloads` | `STORAGE_PRESIGN_DOWNLOADS` | bool | `false` | `presignDownloads` answers blob downloads with a 307 redirect to a presigned URL (s3 and gcs only) instead of streaming them. A repository can override it with presign_downloads. |
| `storage.presignMinSize` | `STORAGE_PRESIGN_MIN_SIZE` | int | `1048576` | `presignMinSize` is the size in bytes below which blobs are always streamed; 0 redirects everything and a negative value is rejected at startup. |
| `storage.presignEndpoint` | `STORAGE_PRESIGN_ENDPOINT` | string | `empty` | `presignEndpoint` is the public base URL (absolute http(s), no query or fragment) that presigned URLs are signed against (S3 family); empty uses the endpoint. Set it when the endpoint is not reachable by clients. |
| `storage.gcsBucket` | `OPENARTIFACT_GCS_BUCKET` | string | `empty` | `gcsBucket` is the GCS bucket (reached through the S3-compatible XML API). |
| `storage.gcsHmacKey` | `OPENARTIFACT_GCS_HMAC_KEY` | string | `empty` | `gcsHmacKey` is the GCS HMAC access key (required for gcs). |
| `storage.gcsHmacSecret` | `OPENARTIFACT_GCS_HMAC_SECRET` | string | `empty` | **Secret.** `gcsHmacSecret` is the GCS HMAC secret. |
| `storage.azureAccountName` | `OPENARTIFACT_AZURE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | string | `empty` | `azureAccountName` is the Azure storage account name. |
| `storage.azureAccountKey` | `OPENARTIFACT_AZURE_ACCOUNT_KEY` | string | `empty` | **Secret.** `azureAccountKey` is the Azure storage account key. |
| `storage.azureContainerName` | `OPENARTIFACT_AZURE_CONTAINER_NAME` | string | `empty` | `azureContainerName` is the Azure container name. |
| `storage.azureEndpoint` | `OPENARTIFACT_AZURE_ENDPOINT` | string | `empty` | `azureEndpoint` is the blob service URL, for Azurite or a sovereign cloud; empty uses https://\<account>.blob.core.windows.net. |
| `storage.stagingPath` | `STORAGE_STAGING_PATH` | string | `empty` | `stagingPath` is the spool directory for server-relayed presigned uploads on oci storage (filesystem uses \<path>/staging); empty means \<tmp>/openartifact-staging. |
| `storage.ociInsecure` | `STORAGE_OCI_INSECURE` | bool | `false` | `ociInsecure` allows plain HTTP to the OCI registry (dev and testing only). |
| `storage.ociUsername` | `STORAGE_OCI_USERNAME` | string | `empty` | `ociUsername` is the OCI registry user. |
| `storage.ociPassword` | `STORAGE_OCI_PASSWORD` | string | `empty` | **Secret.** `ociPassword` is the OCI registry password. |

### `storage.replica`

`storage.replica` is the optional blob replica: an asynchronous second copy of every blob on another backend (see [operations/replication.md](../operations/replication.md)).

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `storage.replica.type` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_TYPE` | string | `empty` | `type` selects the storage backend: filesystem, s3, gcs, azure, garage, seaweedfs or oci. garage and seaweedfs reuse the S3 client with path-style addressing forced on. |
| `storage.replica.endpoint` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_ENDPOINT` | string | `empty` | `endpoint` is the endpoint URL of an S3-compatible service (s3, garage, seaweedfs) or the URL of the OCI registry. |
| `storage.replica.bucket` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_BUCKET` | string | `empty` | `bucket` is the bucket name (s3, garage, seaweedfs) or the OCI repository prefix. |
| `storage.replica.region` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_REGION` | string | `us-east-1` | `region` is the AWS region or equivalent. |
| `storage.replica.accessKey` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_ACCESS_KEY` | string | `empty` | `accessKey` is the S3 access key. It is used only when both keys are set, otherwise the AWS credential chain applies. |
| `storage.replica.secretKey` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_SECRET_KEY` | string | `empty` | **Secret.** `secretKey` is the S3 secret key. |
| `storage.replica.path` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_PATH` | string | `empty` | `path` is the directory of the filesystem backend. |
| `storage.replica.options` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_OPTIONS` | map | `empty` | `options` are free-form backend options. The environment form is comma-separated key=value pairs, merged over the YAML keys. None of the built-in backends reads any key yet. |
| `storage.replica.forcePathStyle` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_FORCE_PATH_STYLE` | bool | `false` | `forcePathStyle` uses path-style S3 addressing (required for MinIO, Garage and SeaweedFS). |
| `storage.replica.gcsBucket` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_GCS_BUCKET` | string | `empty` | `gcsBucket` is the GCS bucket (reached through the S3-compatible XML API). |
| `storage.replica.gcsHmacKey` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_GCS_HMAC_KEY` | string | `empty` | `gcsHmacKey` is the GCS HMAC access key (required for gcs). |
| `storage.replica.gcsHmacSecret` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_GCS_HMAC_SECRET` | string | `empty` | **Secret.** `gcsHmacSecret` is the GCS HMAC secret. |
| `storage.replica.azureAccountName` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_AZURE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | string | `empty` | `azureAccountName` is the Azure storage account name. |
| `storage.replica.azureAccountKey` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_AZURE_ACCOUNT_KEY` | string | `empty` | **Secret.** `azureAccountKey` is the Azure storage account key. |
| `storage.replica.azureContainerName` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_AZURE_CONTAINER_NAME` | string | `empty` | `azureContainerName` is the Azure container name. |
| `storage.replica.azureEndpoint` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_AZURE_ENDPOINT` | string | `empty` | `azureEndpoint` is the blob service URL, for Azurite or a sovereign cloud; empty uses https://\<account>.blob.core.windows.net. |
| `storage.replica.ociInsecure` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_OCI_INSECURE` | bool | `false` | `ociInsecure` allows plain HTTP to the OCI registry (dev and testing only). |
| `storage.replica.ociUsername` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_OCI_USERNAME` | string | `empty` | `ociUsername` is the OCI registry user. |
| `storage.replica.ociPassword` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_OCI_PASSWORD` | string | `empty` | **Secret.** `ociPassword` is the OCI registry password. |
| `storage.replica.readFallback` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_READ_FALLBACK` | string | `notfound` | `readFallback` is what a read does when the primary cannot answer: notfound (the default: the primary says the blob does not exist), error (also when the primary fails) or off (never read from the replica). |
| `storage.replica.interval` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_INTERVAL` | duration | `5s` | `interval` is the pause between replication passes (queued blobs are also picked up as soon as they are enqueued). |
| `storage.replica.batch` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_BATCH` | int | `100` | `batch` is how many queued operations one claim takes. |
| `storage.replica.concurrency` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_CONCURRENCY` | int | `4` | `concurrency` is how many blobs are copied at once. |
| `storage.replica.verifyInterval` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_VERIFY_INTERVAL` | duration | `24h` | `verifyInterval` is the pause between verify passes; 0 = only on demand (POST /api/v1/admin/storage/replication/verify). |
| `storage.replica.verifyDeep` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_VERIFY_DEEP` | bool | `false` | `verifyDeep` also hashes the bytes of both copies during a verify pass, instead of comparing existence and size only. |
| `storage.replica.maxBackoff` | `OPENARTIFACT_STORAGE_REPLICA_MAX_BACKOFF` | duration | `1h` | `maxBackoff` caps the retry delay of a failing operation. |

## log

`log` configures the log level, format and destination.

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `log.level` | `LOG_LEVEL` | string | `info` | `level` is the minimum severity logged: debug, info, warn or error. Unknown values fall back to info. |
| `log.format` | `LOG_FORMAT` | string | `json` | `format` is json or text; any other value gives console text. |
| `log.output` | `LOG_OUTPUT` | string | `stdout` | `output` is stdout, stderr or a file path (appended to). |

## gpg

`gpg` configures the key file that signs APT and RPM metadata and release bundle manifests (see [security/signing.md](../security/signing.md)).

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gpg.enabled` | `GPG_ENABLED` | bool | `false` | `enabled` loads the file key at keyPath. Keys managed through the admin API sign regardless. |
| `gpg.keyPath` | `GPG_KEY_PATH` | string | `empty` | `keyPath` is the private key file (the read-only fallback key). |
| `gpg.passphrase` | `GPG_PASSPHRASE` | string | `empty` | **Secret.** `passphrase` unlocks the key at keyPath. |
| `gpg.autoGenerate` | `GPG_AUTO_GENERATE` | bool | `false` | `autoGenerate` generates an RSA-4096 global signing key at startup when no key exists yet. It needs `OPENARTIFACT_SECRET_KEY` and is replica-safe. |

## attestation

`attestation` configures the signing key of SBOM and VEX attestations (see [security/sbom.md](../security/sbom.md)).

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attestation.keyPath` | `ATTESTATION_KEY_PATH` | string | `empty` | `keyPath` is an unencrypted PKCS#8 or SEC1 PEM private key (ECDSA or Ed25519). Empty: a P-256 key is generated on first use and stored encrypted in the database. |

## auth

`auth` configures sessions, anonymous reads and the login-state and SAML service provider keys (see [security/authentication.md](../security/authentication.md)).

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auth.allowAnonymousRead` | `ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_READ` | bool | `false` | `allowAnonymousRead` lets anonymous clients read private repositories (via the "anonymous-read" permission target). Repositories flagged public are always anonymously readable, never writable, whatever this says. |
| `auth.legacyApiKeyEnabled` | `LEGACY_API_KEY_ENABLED` | bool | `false` | `legacyApiKeyEnabled` accepts the deprecated server.apiKey on write endpoints. |
| `auth.sessionDurationHours` | `SESSION_DURATION_HOURS` | int | `24` | `sessionDurationHours` is the lifetime of a web session, in hours. |
| `auth.hmacKey` | `AUTH_HMAC_KEY` | string | `empty` | **Secret.** `hmacKey` signs OIDC and SAML login state. Unset: a random key is generated once and persisted in system_settings (shared by replicas); a configured value wins. |
| `auth.samlSpCert` | `OPENARTIFACT_SAML_SP_CERT` | string | `empty` | `samlSpCert` is the PEM certificate of the SAML service provider. Unset: a self-signed pair is generated once and persisted encrypted in system_settings (shared by replicas); regenerating it means re-registering the certificate at the identity provider. |
| `auth.samlSpKey` | `OPENARTIFACT_SAML_SP_KEY` | string | `empty` | **Secret.** `samlSpKey` is the PEM private key of the SAML service provider. Unset together with the certificate: a self-signed pair is generated (see samlSpCert). Stored unencrypted while `OPENARTIFACT_SECRET_KEY` is unset. |

## backup

`backup` configures where backups are written and how long a running backup holds back blob deletions (see [operations/backup.md](../operations/backup.md)).

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `backup.backupDir` | `OPENARTIFACT_BACKUP_DIR` | string | `/var/lib/openartifact/backups` | `backupDir` is the directory backup files are written to. |
| `backup.leaseTtl` | `OPENARTIFACT_BACKUP_LEASE_TTL` | duration | `5m` | `leaseTtl` is how long a running backup's hold on deleted blob bytes survives without a heartbeat. A running backup renews it every third of this; a crashed backup stops holding deletions back once it expires. |

## ai

`ai` configures AI-assisted package analysis (see [integrations/ai-analysis.md](../integrations/ai-analysis.md)).

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ai.enabled` | `AI_ENABLED` | bool | `false` | `enabled` turns AI-assisted artifact analysis on (metadata tagging, license check, security notes). |
| `ai.autoAnalyze` | `AI_AUTO_ANALYZE` | bool | `false` | `autoAnalyze` analyses every upload without being asked. Off: analyses start only on request (UI, API or MCP). Needs enabled. |
| `ai.provider` | `AI_PROVIDER` | string | `openai` | `provider` is the LLM backend: openai, azure, ollama or custom (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; needs baseUrl). |
| `ai.baseUrl` | `AI_BASE_URL` | string | `empty` | `baseUrl` overrides the API base URL (Azure OpenAI, Ollama or a custom endpoint). |
| `ai.apiKey` | `AI_API_KEY` | string | `empty` | **Secret.** `apiKey` authenticates to the provider; required for openai and azure, leave it empty for a local ollama. |
| `ai.model` | `AI_MODEL` | string | `gpt-4o-mini` | `model` is the model to use, for example gpt-4o-mini or llama3; it must be available on the configured provider. |
| `ai.maxTokens` | `AI_MAX_TOKENS` | int | `1024` | `maxTokens` caps the completion tokens of one analysis request. |
| `ai.timeoutSecs` | `AI_TIMEOUT_SECS` | int | `30` | `timeoutSecs` is the HTTP timeout of an AI API call, in seconds. |
| `ai.systemPrompt` | `AI_SYSTEM_PROMPT` | string | `empty` | `systemPrompt` overrides the built-in system prompt; empty uses it. |

## mcp

`mcp` configures the embedded Model Context Protocol server (see [integrations/mcp.md](../integrations/mcp.md)).

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mcp.enabled` | `MCP_ENABLED` | bool | `false` | `enabled` mounts the MCP server on the main HTTP listener. |
| `mcp.transport` | `MCP_TRANSPORT` | string | `http` | `transport` must be http (the only supported transport; stdio is rejected). The endpoint requires an "Authorization: Bearer" token. |
| `mcp.httpPath` | `MCP_HTTP_PATH` | string | `/mcp` | `httpPath` is the mount path of the HTTP endpoint. |
| `mcp.allowedOrigins` | `MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | list | `empty` | `allowedOrigins` are the browser origins (scheme://host[:port]) accepted in the Origin header of MCP requests, besides the origin of baseUrl. A request with any other Origin is refused with 403; requests without an Origin header (non-browser clients) are unaffected. |
| `mcp.maxBodyBytes` | `MCP_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | int | `1048576` | `maxBodyBytes` caps one MCP request body (default 1 MiB). |
| `mcp.rateLimitPerMinute` | `MCP_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | int | `600` | `rateLimitPerMinute` caps MCP requests per authenticated principal per minute (default 600; 0 disables the limit). |
| `mcp.aiTriggerPerMinute` | `MCP_AI_TRIGGER_PER_MINUTE` | int | `10` | `aiTriggerPerMinute` caps trigger_ai_analysis calls per principal per minute, since each one can cost an LLM call (default 10; 0 disables). |

## workers

`workers` tunes the background workers: metadata regeneration, Docker registry garbage collection and upload staging, webhook retention.

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `workers.metadataRegenConcurrency` | `OPENARTIFACT_METADATA_REGEN_CONCURRENCY` | int | `4` | `metadataRegenConcurrency` caps how many metadata regenerations (npm, maven, deb, rpm together) run at once. Each pins up to two database connections, so keep it well below database.maxOpenConns. |
| `workers.dockerGcInterval` | `OPENARTIFACT_DOCKER_GC_INTERVAL` | duration | `1h` | `dockerGcInterval` is the pause between scheduled Docker registry garbage collection passes (untagged manifests and the blobs only they used). Zero or negative disables the schedule; the admin API can still run it. |
| `workers.dockerGcGracePeriod` | `OPENARTIFACT_DOCKER_GC_GRACE_PERIOD` | duration | `24h` | `dockerGcGracePeriod` is how long an untagged manifest, or an unreferenced blob, must have been idle before registry GC may delete it. It must outlast the slowest push: layers are uploaded before the manifest that references them. |
| `workers.proxyDockerDigestTtl` | `OPENARTIFACT_PROXY_DOCKER_DIGEST_TTL` | duration | `720h` | `proxyDockerDigestTtl` is how long a docker proxy keeps a manifest or blob addressed by digest after its last pull. Such content never changes, so this only bounds the cache's size: the proxy cache worker evicts what has not been pulled for this long, and the next pull fetches it again. Zero keeps it until an admin purge or the repository's removal. |
| `workers.dockerUploadTtl` | `OPENARTIFACT_DOCKER_UPLOAD_TTL` | duration | `24h` | `dockerUploadTtl` is how long a blob upload session may sit idle before the sweeper deletes it and its staged file. Zero or negative disables the sweeper. |
| `workers.dockerUploadDir` | `OPENARTIFACT_DOCKER_UPLOAD_DIR` | string | `empty` | `dockerUploadDir` is where in-progress blob uploads are staged. Empty means /tmp/openartifact/docker-uploads. |
| `workers.webhookDeliveryRetentionDays` | `OPENARTIFACT_WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_RETENTION_DAYS` | int | `30` | `webhookDeliveryRetentionDays` is how many days finished (success or failed) webhook delivery records are kept before the hourly purge deletes them. 0 keeps them forever. Pending deliveries are never purged. |

## trash

`trash` tunes soft delete (see [operations/trash.md](../operations/trash.md)).

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trash.retentionDays` | `OPENARTIFACT_TRASH_RETENTION` | int | `7` | `retentionDays` is how many days a deleted artifact, version or repository stays restorable before the purge worker removes it for good. It applies to repositories without their own trash_retention_days; 0 disables the trash (deletes are immediate and permanent). |
| `trash.purgeInterval` | `OPENARTIFACT_TRASH_PURGE_INTERVAL` | duration | `15m` | `purgeInterval` is the pause between purge passes. Zero or negative disables the schedule: nothing expires until an admin purges by hand. |

## docs

`docs` configures the links from the web UI to the published documentation.

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `docs.baseUrl` | `OPENARTIFACT_DOCS_BASE_URL` | string | `https://openartifact.github.io/` | `baseUrl` is the root of the published documentation site; the web UI links to the version matching the server (release builds) or to the latest docs (development builds). Point it at an internal mirror for air-gapped installs; empty hides every documentation link. |

## blobDeletion

`blobDeletion` tunes the deferred deletion of blob bytes (see [operations/storage.md](../operations/storage.md)).

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `blobDeletion.grace` | `OPENARTIFACT_BLOB_DELETION_GRACE` | duration | `24h` | `grace` is how long the bytes of a deleted blob are kept before they may be removed. During it a re-upload of the same content reuses them. Zero removes them as soon as no running backup needs them. |
| `blobDeletion.sweepInterval` | `OPENARTIFACT_BLOB_DELETION_SWEEP_INTERVAL` | duration | `1m` | `sweepInterval` is the pause between sweeper passes. Zero or negative disables the schedule (the queue then only grows). |
| `blobDeletion.sweepBatch` | `OPENARTIFACT_BLOB_DELETION_SWEEP_BATCH` | int | `200` | `sweepBatch` is how many queued deletions a sweeper claims at a time. |

## tiering

`tiering` tunes the storage tier mover (see [operations/storage-tiering.md](../operations/storage-tiering.md)). Tiers and policies themselves are managed through the admin API; with no tier besides the primary store configured none of this has any effect.

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tiering.enabled` | `OPENARTIFACT_TIERING_ENABLED` | bool | `true` | `enabled` switches the background mover on. Reads from every tier work regardless; only the movement of blobs between tiers depends on it. |
| `tiering.interval` | `OPENARTIFACT_TIERING_INTERVAL` | duration | `5m` | `interval` is the pause between mover passes. Zero or negative disables the schedule; an admin can still start a pass by hand. |
| `tiering.batch` | `OPENARTIFACT_TIERING_BATCH` | int | `200` | `batch` caps how many blobs one pass moves; the rest wait for the next pass. |
| `tiering.concurrency` | `OPENARTIFACT_TIERING_CONCURRENCY` | int | `2` | `concurrency` is how many blobs are copied at once. |
| `tiering.maxBytesPerSecond` | `OPENARTIFACT_TIERING_MAX_BYTES_PER_SECOND` | int | `67108864` | `maxBytesPerSecond` caps the mover's total copy bandwidth (all concurrent copies together). Zero is unlimited. |
| `tiering.verifyReadback` | `OPENARTIFACT_TIERING_VERIFY_READBACK` | bool | `true` | `verifyReadback` re-reads each copied blob from the target tier and compares its sha256 before the placement flips, on top of the size check. |
| `tiering.accessFlushInterval` | `OPENARTIFACT_TIERING_ACCESS_FLUSH_INTERVAL` | duration | `30s` | `accessFlushInterval` is how often recorded blob downloads (used by "idle for N days" policies and promote-on-read) are written to the database. |
| `tiering.refreshInterval` | `OPENARTIFACT_TIERING_REFRESH_INTERVAL` | duration | `30s` | `refreshInterval` is how often each replica reloads the tier list, so a tier created on one replica is used by the others. |

## recovery

`recovery` groups the disaster-recovery settings.

### `recovery.journal`

`recovery.journal` tunes the row journal that mirrors package metadata as sidecar blobs in the blob store (see [operations/rebuild-from-storage.md](../operations/rebuild-from-storage.md)).

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `recovery.journal.enabled` | `OPENARTIFACT_RECOVERY_JOURNAL_ENABLED` | bool | `true` | `enabled` switches the journal on: the database triggers mark changed rows and the worker writes their sidecar blobs. Off, nothing is captured and `openartifact rebuild` cannot restore rows created while it was off. |
| `recovery.journal.interval` | `OPENARTIFACT_RECOVERY_JOURNAL_INTERVAL` | duration | `10s` | `interval` is the pause between worker passes that drain the dirty queue. |
| `recovery.journal.batch` | `OPENARTIFACT_RECOVERY_JOURNAL_BATCH` | int | `200` | `batch` is how many dirty rows one drain step claims. |
| `recovery.journal.concurrency` | `OPENARTIFACT_RECOVERY_JOURNAL_CONCURRENCY` | int | `4` | `concurrency` is how many sidecar blobs are written or deleted at once. |
| `recovery.journal.reconcileInterval` | `OPENARTIFACT_RECOVERY_JOURNAL_RECONCILE_INTERVAL` | duration | `24h` | `reconcileInterval` is how often every journaled table is re-checked for rows without a sidecar (backfill) and sidecars without a row. Zero disables periodic reconciles after the first complete one. |

## projects

`projects` tunes project self-service (see [security/projects.md](../security/projects.md)).

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `projects.selfCreate` | `OPENARTIFACT_PROJECTS_SELF_CREATE` | bool | `false` | `selfCreate` lets any authenticated human user create a project and become its owner. Off by default: only global admins create projects. An administrator can change it at runtime (system setting projects.self_create), which then takes precedence over this default. |

## federation

`federation` tunes federated repositories (see [operations/federation.md](../operations/federation.md)). Repositories are federated individually through the admin API; this only switches the pull workers and the peer endpoints on and tunes them.

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `federation.enabled` | `OPENARTIFACT_FEDERATION_ENABLED` | bool | `false` | `enabled` starts the pull workers and mounts the /federation/v1 peer endpoints. Off by default. |
| `federation.pollInterval` | `OPENARTIFACT_FEDERATION_POLL_INTERVAL` | duration | `30s` | `pollInterval` is the pause between pulls of one peer that is caught up. |
| `federation.batchSize` | `OPENARTIFACT_FEDERATION_BATCH_SIZE` | int | `200` | `batchSize` is how many log entries one pull page carries. |
| `federation.maxBackoff` | `OPENARTIFACT_FEDERATION_MAX_BACKOFF` | duration | `15m` | `maxBackoff` caps the retry delay of an unreachable or failing peer. |
| `federation.requestTimeout` | `OPENARTIFACT_FEDERATION_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` | duration | `30s` | `requestTimeout` bounds one request to a peer (blob transfers are bounded by it per request, not in total). |
| `federation.tombstoneRetention` | `OPENARTIFACT_FEDERATION_TOMBSTONE_RETENTION` | duration | `720h` | `tombstoneRetention` is how long the tombstone of a deleted unit is kept in the log; a member that stays offline longer must be resynced. |

## telemetry

`telemetry` configures OpenTelemetry export (off by default), see [operations/monitoring.md](../operations/monitoring.md).

### `telemetry.otlp`

`telemetry.otlp` configures the OTLP exporters. The standard `OTEL_*` environment variables override the file; signal specific `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_*` variables only apply while endpoint is empty.

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `telemetry.otlp.enabled` | `OPENARTIFACT_OTLP_ENABLED` | bool | `false` | `enabled` turns tracing on. Off by default; `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true` forces it off. |
| `telemetry.otlp.endpoint` | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | string | `empty` | `endpoint` is host:port or an http(s) URL of the collector. Empty uses the SDK default (localhost:4317 for grpc, localhost:4318 for http). |
| `telemetry.otlp.protocol` | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` | string | `grpc` | `protocol` is "grpc" (default) or "http" (OTLP/HTTP protobuf). |
| `telemetry.otlp.headers` | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` | map | `empty` | **Secret.** `headers` are sent with every export request (collector credentials). Never logged. The environment form is comma-separated key=value pairs with percent-encoded values. |
| `telemetry.otlp.insecure` | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_INSECURE` | bool | `false` | `insecure` disables TLS towards the collector. An http:// endpoint implies it. |
| `telemetry.otlp.serviceName` | `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | string | `openartifact` | `serviceName` is the service.name resource attribute. |
| `telemetry.otlp.sampleRatio` | `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG` | float | `1` | `sampleRatio` is the fraction of new traces recorded, in [0,1]. Requests carrying a sampled traceparent are always recorded (parent based). |
| `telemetry.otlp.metrics` | `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` | bool | `false` | `metrics` additionally exports the Prometheus registry (Go runtime and openartifact_* families) over OTLP to the same endpoint. /metrics is unaffected. The environment form is `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER`: otlp turns it on, none turns it off. |

## scanners

`scanners` configures the external vulnerability scanners (trivy, grype) used by on-demand scans (see [security/scanning.md](../security/scanning.md)). OSV needs none of it.

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scanners.cacheDir` | `OPENARTIFACT_SCANNER_CACHE_DIR` | string | `empty` | `cacheDir` is where the scanners keep their vulnerability databases (\<cacheDir>/trivy, \<cacheDir>/grype). It must be writable unless offline is set. Empty means a directory under the user cache dir; the container image sets /var/cache/openartifact/scanners. |
| `scanners.updateInterval` | `OPENARTIFACT_SCANNER_UPDATE_INTERVAL` | duration | `6h` | `updateInterval` is the pause between database refreshes. 0 downloads only when the server starts and never again; otherwise at least 1h. |
| `scanners.offline` | `OPENARTIFACT_SCANNER_OFFLINE` | bool | `false` | `offline` stops the server from downloading databases: scans use what cacheDir already holds and fail while it holds none. |
| `scanners.downloadBaseUrl` | `OPENARTIFACT_SCANNER_DOWNLOAD_BASE_URL` | string | `https://github.com` | `downloadBaseUrl` is the https origin the pinned release archives are downloaded from when a scanner's install mode is "auto". A mirror must serve GitHub's release paths (/\<owner>/\<repo>/releases/download/\<tag>/\<file>). |

### `scanners.trivy`

`scanners.trivy` configures the trivy binary and its database sources.

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scanners.trivy.path` | `OPENARTIFACT_TRIVY_PATH` | string | `empty` | `path` is the binary: a command name looked up on PATH, or an absolute path. Empty means "trivy". |
| `scanners.trivy.install` | `OPENARTIFACT_TRIVY_INSTALL` | string | `none` | `install` is "none" (default) or "auto": download the pinned trivy release into the cache directory when path is empty and trivy is not on PATH. |
| `scanners.trivy.dbRepository` | `OPENARTIFACT_TRIVY_DB_REPOSITORY` | string | `empty` | `dbRepository` is an OCI repository mirroring ghcr.io/aquasecurity/trivy-db. Empty is the upstream default. |
| `scanners.trivy.javaDbRepository` | `OPENARTIFACT_TRIVY_JAVA_DB_REPOSITORY` | string | `empty` | `javaDbRepository` is an OCI repository mirroring ghcr.io/aquasecurity/trivy-java-db. Empty does not download the Java database (several hundred MB; only JAR scanning needs it). |

### `scanners.grype`

`scanners.grype` configures the grype binary and its database source.

| YAML key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scanners.grype.path` | `OPENARTIFACT_GRYPE_PATH` | string | `empty` | `path` is the binary: a command name looked up on PATH, or an absolute path. Empty means "grype". |
| `scanners.grype.install` | `OPENARTIFACT_GRYPE_INSTALL` | string | `none` | `install` is "none" (default) or "auto": download the pinned grype release into the cache directory when path is empty and grype is not on PATH. |
| `scanners.grype.dbUrl` | `OPENARTIFACT_GRYPE_DB_URL` | string | `empty` | `dbUrl` is the database listing URL of a mirror (`GRYPE_DB_UPDATE_URL`). Empty is the upstream default. |

## Environment-only variables

These variables are read by the configuration loader but have no YAML key.

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED` | `true` forces telemetry off, overriding `telemetry.otlp.enabled` and `OPENARTIFACT_OTLP_ENABLED`. |

Variables read outside the configuration loader, such as the secret-encryption key, the metrics scrape token and the migration switch, are described in [Environment-only variables](../getting-started/configuration.md#environment-only-variables).
